elites.name: autodidactic_world_model_science
elites.title: Autodidactic World Models for Automated Scientific Discovery in Uncharted Territories
elites.short_hypothesis: AI systems will develop self-sufficient world models to autonomously formulate, test, and refine scientific hypotheses in domains entirely unknown to human knowledge.
elites.abstract: Future AI research will focus on creating agents that learn to build comprehensive, dynamic world models from scratch, enabling them to independently explore scientific frontiers. These agents will not only discover novel phenomena but also invent the very scientific methodologies required to understand them, bridging the gap between open-ended discovery and automated scientific progress.

elites.name: recursive-world-model-science
elites.title: Recursive World Model Refinement for Automated Scientific Discovery
elites.short_hypothesis: AI systems capable of autonomously and recursively refining their internal world models will accelerate scientific discovery by enabling more efficient hypothesis generation, experimental design, and data interpretation.
elites.abstract: Future AI systems must move beyond static world models to dynamically update and improve their understanding of the physical and abstract world based on new observations and experimental results. This recursive refinement process, inspired by scientific progress itself, will unlock new avenues for automated scientific discovery by allowing AI to autonomously identify knowledge gaps, propose novel experiments, and interpret complex data with increasing sophistication.

elites.name: creative_problem_solving_in_novel_domains
elites.title: Generalizing Creative Problem Solving to Unforeseen Domains
elites.short_hypothesis: Developing AI systems capable of creative problem-solving that can generalize to entirely novel and unforeseen domains, rather than being confined to pre-defined task categories, is a key frontier for open-ended intelligence.
elites.abstract: This research will focus on creating AI agents that can go beyond solving known types of anomalous problems to invent novel solutions for problems in domains they have never encountered, demonstrating true creative adaptation and problem formulation. The aim is to achieve a level of creative problem-solving that mirrors human ingenuity in its breadth and adaptability.

elites.name: recursive-world-model-science-safety
elites.title: Safety Frameworks for Self-Improving World Models in Automated Science
elites.short_hypothesis: Ensuring the safety of AI systems that recursively improve their own world models for scientific discovery requires novel oversight mechanisms that can validate emergent scientific hypotheses and reasoning chains.
elites.abstract: As AI systems like The AI Scientist-v2 demonstrate increasing autonomy in scientific discovery, the development of self-improving world models presents a critical safety challenge. New frameworks are needed to monitor and control the iterative refinement of these internal representations of reality, ensuring that the scientific knowledge generated remains grounded in verifiable evidence and aligned with human scientific understanding.

elites.name: emergent_self_assembling_scientific_ecosystems
elites.title: Emergent Self-Assembling Scientific Ecosystems Driven by Artificial Life Principles
elites.short_hypothesis: Applying principles from artificial life, AI agents will autonomously form complex, self-organizing 'ecosystems' that collectively drive scientific discovery through emergent division of labor and symbiotic knowledge generation.
elites.abstract: Instead of monolithic AI scientists, future systems will comprise diverse, specialized agents that co-evolve and interact, akin to biological ecosystems, to tackle complex scientific problems. This emergent division of labor and symbiotic knowledge exchange will unlock novel discovery pathways currently inaccessible to single, albeit powerful, AI entities.
